correctness.rationale: Proof starts from the precise a=b=1/4, M=2 volume-preserving map. For center-only observables the full covariance equals the reduced \(P^n\) covariance (Takahasi--Tsujii 2024, Section 3.5). Binary Rademacher expansion of c-1/2 yields summable coefficients -2^{-j-1}, and P acts as the killed fair walk on positive levels. The recurrence with zero boundary has the unique summable solution w_j=-(2^{-j}-eta^j)/(2(1-5z/4)). Evaluating its inner product proves the exact algebraic generating function. z=4/5 is removable because eta(4/5)=1/2; the only modulus-one singularities at +/-1 have respective square-root coefficients -2sqrt(2) and -2sqrt(2)/81, giving sqrt(2/pi)(1+(-1)^n/81)\(n^{-3/2}\)+O(\(n^{-5/2}\)). Exact-rational computations independently agree through 25 coefficients and parity asymptotic numerics support normalization, but the infinite proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Exact same-map primary manuscript arXiv:2408.16618v1 supplies general order \(n^{-3/2}\) and an exact killed-walk kernel; it does not provide the all-lag Green function for the natural center coordinate or the two distinct sharp parity amplitudes. Related 2023 exponential mixing excludes the neutral parameter, and 2024 periodic-index analysis and published matching-family mathematical records concern different invariants. The claimed contribution is an evaluated infinite geometric resolvent and its two-edge transfer, not discovery of the walk kernel or of the decay exponent. Unindexed equivalent spectral computations remain possible.
residual_risks: The 2024 random-walk kernel determines individual levels and an independently performed infinite sum could yield equivalent constants; an unindexed prior Green-function evaluation cannot be ruled out by searches.
Only indexed summary rather than full manuscript was checked for the two neighboring published neutral-periodic-fiber records; their stated objects and invariants differ.

value.rationale: A natural Lipschitz physical observable in an established nonuniformly hyperbolic, volume-preserving map receives its complete algebraic covariance generating function and sharp parity-resolved mixing constants. This answers a finer quantitative question left by the source bounds, reveals the contribution of the negative spectral edge, and gives a reproducible benchmark for the neutral-center polynomial-mixing mechanism. It is not an arbitrary finite parameter sample and no broad general-observable theorem is asserted.
